newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUX SOARS TO 4TH CLOSING HIGH IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: BUX SOARS TO 4TH CLOSING HIGH IN A ROW.

text.p: Hungary's good economic performance and a strong dollar were the main factors behind a fourth successive closing high of the BUX index on Monday, traders and analysts said.
The BUX index closed at a preliminary 7,631.42 points, up 25.82 points or 0.34 percent.
"Certainly the strong dollar is a factor," said Nigel Rendell, analyst with HSBC in London. "Also, there is a lot of foreign buying...because of the recovery of the Hungarian economy".
One Budapest trader said that although today's gain was not substantial, there was a fairly steady and sustained buying interest.
"There is steady demand for TVK and MOL, for example," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities.
MOL edged up 25 forints to close at 4,380 and TVK also advanced 25 forints to 4,000.
Nagy added that part of Monday's rise could also be explained by the fact that market players bought shares in order to sell (BUX index) futures because of the high interest content of the latter.
Nagy added that the strong dollar, which makes Hungarian shares cheap to foreign investors, was also a factor that sustained the market.
He said, however, that a wait-and-see attitude was obvious and turnover would only pick up as companies' first half results arrive.
These are due by August 15 and so far only two firms have submitted them.
Rendell said that although he still expected a good performance from the Budapest Stock Exchange this year, first half results were unlikely to trigger significant price rises.
"Unless there are exceptional surprises, I don't think the corporate numbers will have a great impact on the market for the time being," he said.
